paras: The shooting of Cuff, alias Henry Brooks, took place at Lake City, Florida, on a Wednesday afternoon in August 1881, when a deputy sheriff and a man he had summoned fired on Brooks, a Black man, as he fled arrest. A pistol ball struck him in the back of the head without serious harm, and he was captured and held under a justice's warrant.

According to the Lake City Reporter, Brooks was "a strange negro" in the town who had been charged with "a serious offense." The paper did not name the charge but repeated a rumor that he had committed some crime at Crawfordsville, Florida, and had left there on that account.

Deputy Sheriff Bethea summoned Henry Waite, whom the paper described as "a negro," to help him, and the two went to the house where Brooks was staying in the eastern part of town. The deputy took one door and Waite another, and they called for Brooks, who appeared frightened and jumped out of the door near Waite. When Brooks kept running after Waite called on him to halt, both men opened fire, and one pistol ball struck him in the back of the head but, in the paper's words, "did no damage."
Gold Champion, described as "another negro," joined the pursuit and captured Brooks at the edge of Lake DeSoto.
Brooks was then held in custody under a warrant issued by Justice A. J. Henry. No report of the charge being tried, or of any inquiry into the shooting, appears in the coverage.

The only known account is a short Lake City Reporter item that the Savannah Morning News reprinted on August 31, 1881, in a front-page roundup of Florida newspaper items. It ran without a headline or comment among notes on land sales, fires and new businesses, and directly above a longer Lake City item on an armed attack on a local man's house. The item identified Brooks, Waite and Champion by race, called both shooters "officers," and gave only the officers' side of the arrest.
